label: RB2011UiAS-2HnD-IN
description: MikroTik RB2011UiAS-2HnD-IN (RB2011UiAS-2HnD-IN) - 5x 100M and 5x 1G RJ45, 1x SFP, Wi-Fi 2.4 GHz. Powered by the DC jack or by passive PoE-in on eth1 only (8-30 V, not 802.3af); passive PoE-out on eth10.
notes: Vendor rows read 2026-11-28 from https://mikrotik.com/product/RB2011UiAS-2HnD-IN: **PoE in Passive PoE**, **PoE in input Voltage 8-30 V**, **Max power consumption 11 W**, **PoE-out ports Ether10**, **PoE out Passive PoE**. The user manual, https://help.mikrotik.com/docs/spaces/UM/pages/16351574/RB2011UiAS-2HnD-IN (read 2026-11-28), names the socket and the standard: "The device accepts powering from either the power jack or from the LAN1 Ethernet port ... Eth1 port accepts 8-30 V DC input ... from non-standard (passive) Power over Ethernet injectors. The board does not work with IEEE802.3af compliant 48 V power injectors." So `eth1` draws the 11 W board ceiling; `eth2`-`eth9` declare poeIn: false; `eth10` is passive PoE-out only. The eight sockets beside the inlet had been inheriting the 12.95 W 802.3af guess from `category: wireless` - on a board whose own manual says it will not run from an 802.3af injector.
